title: Tenant impact matrix and maintenance templates
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact playbook and communication templates for tenant-facing maintenance and upgrades for private deployments (VPC / on-prem). This doc combines: (1) a tenant-impact matrix to quickly classify who is affected and how; (2) customer-facing notice templates (email + Slack + portal banner); (3) short Terraform module change notes and migration hints; (4) a phased upgrade plan with verification and rollback criteria; (5) an internal pre/post checklist for SRE and customer success.

Audience:
- Solutions engineering and customer success owners for tenant customers
- SRE/Platform engineers executing private upgrades
- Account teams that need to coordinate consent/blackout windows

High-level approach (summary):
1) Classify: quickly map upgrade changes to tenant-impact categories (no-impact, config-only, brief-restart, rolling-restart, tenant-visible-db-migration).
2) Communicate: use the templates below tailored to the category; include explicit SLO impact, expected downtime window, and post-upgrade verification steps.
3) Schedule: coordinate windows by tenant timezone and blackout requests; prefer low-traffic regional windows when possible.
4) Execute: staged canary -> 10% wave -> 50% wave -> full. Automated health checks gate progression.
5) Verify & Close: run verification checklist; record artifacts and notify tenant CS.

Tenant impact matrix (quick reference):
- No-impact: purely control-plane metadata, zero restarts, no client action. Template: "No action required".
- Config-only: config reload required on hosts, rolling reload possible, short token-level lag <30s. Template: "Brief note + scheduled window".
- Brief-restart: process restart (1–3 hosts) per tenant pool, typical interruption <2 minutes per request path. Template: "Maintenance window with retry guidance".
- Rolling-restart: conservative, staggered restarts across nodes, expect tail-latency spikes up to 10s over 10–20 minutes. Template: "Longer window + failover note".
- DB migration / stateful: tenant-facing migrations or KV changes, may require read-only window or queued writes. Template: "Pre-consent required + detailed rollback plan".

Customer-facing notice templates (placeholders in ALL_CAPS):
1) Short pre-notice (30 days / default):
SUBJECT: Upcoming maintenance for your Redwood Private deployment – ACTION OPTIONAL
Hi CUSTOMER_NAME,
Heads-up: we're scheduling maintenance that improves stability and enables new observability features for your private deployment in REGION. This is a CONFIG-ONLY change and does not require action. Planned window: START_DATETIME to END_DATETIME (tenant local). Expected user impact: NONE.
If you have blackout constraints, tell us by BY_DATE and we will accommodate.
Thanks,
Sofia and the Private Deployments team

2) Technical pre-notice (7 days):
SUBJECT: Maintenance: brief rolling restart planned for YOUR_ORG – please verify integration points
Hi CUSTOMER_NAME,
We plan a rolling restart to roll out kernel fixes to inference workers. Window: START_DATETIME – END_DATETIME. Expected interruption: <2 minutes for in-flight requests per worker; global throughput may be reduced during window.
What you may see: transient 503s, token streaming restarts for long-lived connections.
Action items: ensure your client retries are configured (recommended exponential backoff up to 10s). If you require a hard blackout, reply before BY_DATE.
Post-checks: we will run inference smoke tests and a sample prompt suite scoped to your tenant and share results.
Thanks,
Private Deployments Ops

3) Critical migration notice (pre-consent required):
SUBJECT: Required action: planned read-only migration affecting YOUR_ORG on DATE
Hi CUSTOMER_NAME,
We will perform a state migration to upgrade your tenant KV store. This will place your instance in read-only mode for an estimated DURATION. We require explicit consent to proceed on the scheduled date.
- Why: data format fix that prevents future request corruption.
- Expected impact: READ-ONLY starting at START_DT for UP_TO_DURATION. Writes during that window will return 409.
- Rollback: if we hit blockers, we will attempt an automatic rollback within ROLLBACK_THD minutes; if rollback fails, we will coordinate an emergency plan with you.
Please reply ACCEPT / REJECT by BY_DATE. If no reply, we will default to HOLD and contact you for scheduling.

Portal banner / in-console note (short):
"Maintenance window scheduled START_DATETIME – END_DATETIME. Expect brief interruptions to inference. Contact cs@redwood.ai for blackout requests"

Operator Slack DM template (to CS/AM):
@CS_ONCALL FYI: Running canary for tenant YOUR_ORG at START_DT. Canary health checks: inference smoke, kv consistency, auth checks. Will report status every +10m.

Terraform module notes (concise dev-facing):
- Module bump summary (v1.8 -> v1.9): worker_pool: expose rolling_restart_batch_size, add variable skip_kv_migration (default=false), output cluster_upgrade_state.
- Migration hints: if skip_kv_migration=true, deploy is faster but KV schema remains old; only safe if tenant is constrained and explicit consent obtained.
- Breaking change: variable names changed: "worker_count" -> "replica_count" (backward compatibility wrapper provided for one release).
- Minimal tf apply sequence for safe upgrade:
  1) git tag release/v1.9 and push PR to infra repo referencing module v1.9.
  2) terraform plan with var replica_count and rolling_restart_batch_size tuned to 1 for canary.
  3) tf apply on a single tenant workspace (canary), verify smoke checks, then proceed.

Sample TF snippet (commented):
# use small batch for first waves
module "rdw_private_cluster" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/tf-modules//private-cluster?ref=v1.9"
  replica_count = var.replica_count
  rolling_restart_batch_size = 1  # start small for canary
  skip_kv_migration = false    # require consent to skip
}

Upgrade execution plan (staged):
- Gate 0 (preflight, -7 days): collect blackout windows, confirm CS contact, run dry-run terraform plan (no apply).
- Gate 1 (canary, 1 tenant, 1 host): apply module with batch_size=1, run smoke tests (see verification list). Hold for 30m stable.
- Gate 2 (10% tenants / non-critical): run parallel rolling restarts, batch_size=2, monitor error budget. Hold if 5xx rate > baseline + 1% for 15m.
- Gate 3 (50%): increase parallelism, run extended load tests.
- Gate 4 (full): finish migration for remaining tenants and run final sanity tests.

Rollback criteria (examples):
- Canary failure: persistent 5xx > baseline + 2% for 5 minutes OR failed KV migration verification. Immediate rollback and notification.
- Progressive wave stop conditions: any tenant reporting severe functional regression (customer report + automated test failure) -> pause wave and investigate.

Verification checklist (internal):
- Health checks run and green: inference smoke prompts (3 prompt categories), auth token flow, KV read/write consistency sample.
- Latency: p50 and p95 within SLO budget for tenant baseline (compare 24h pre-window).
- Cost/Utilization: no unexpected GPU OOM or host churn.
- Logs: no increase in error-class "migration-fatal".
- Post-upgrade synthetic test pass (link to test results).
- Customer success acknowledged receipt of post-upgrade summary.

Internal pre-launch checklist (SRE + CS):
- [ ] Confirm CS owner and escalation contact listed on ticket.
- [ ] Collect blackout windows and consent flags; update schedule spreadsheet.
- [ ] Create rollout PR with tf module version and reviewer tags.
- [ ] Update runbook run_id and attach preflight plan.
- [ ] Prepare canary smoke prompt set and test harness.
- [ ] Notify Legal/Compliance for stateful migrations if required.
- [ ] Communicate to on-call channel 24h and 1h before start.

Post-maintenance summary (template):
SUBJECT: Maintenance complete for YOUR_ORG – results and verification
Hi CUSTOMER_NAME,
Maintenance completed at COMPLETION_DATETIME. Summary: rolled upgrade to v1.9, no data loss, smoke tests passed (link). Observed: brief restart spikes at +1.2s p95 for 12 minutes during wave 2, recovered by wave 3. No action required.
If you notice any regression please reply to this thread or open a support ticket referencing MAINTENANCE_ID.

Notes on consent and privacy: stateful migrations require explicit tenant consent. When consent is withheld, we will either schedule an alternate window or enable skip_kv_migration where safe (documented in terraform variables).

Escalation contacts (internal):
- Primary SRE: Arjun Patel (pager)
- Private Deployments Lead: Sofia Martinez (slack)
- CS escalation: Leah Kim (email)
- On-call infra: PagerDuty (link in runbook)

Open questions / TODOs (draft):
- Add a per-tenant health-weight metric to gate automated progression.
- Define default behavior when tenant does not respond to migration consent request (current: HOLD). Consider auto-schedule if explicit opt-in required by contract.
- Add a lightweight consent capture in the Console for future migrations.

Appendix: quick examples of short messages for different channels (copy-paste friendly):
- Email short: "Planned maintenance NEXT_TUE 02:00–04:00 UTC. Expected brief interruptions. Reply for blackout."
- Console banner: "Maintenance in prog: START–END. Expect brief interruptions."
- CS DM: "Canary for YOUR_ORG started. Running smoke suite now. Reporting in 10m."

---
Draft notes: keep this doc intentionally concise. Use as a one-page execution guide + copyable templates for tenant comms. For complex migrations create a dedicated runbook linked in linked_artifacts.
